subject: general
question: Which ministry has introduced a technology-driven initiative called e-Zero FIR on 19 May 2025 to boost India's cybercrime-fighting capabilities?

options.text: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology

solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Home Affairs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)** introduced the technology-driven initiative called **e-Zero FIR** on **19 May 2025**.
 
• The primary objective of e-Zero FIR is to **boost India's cybercrime-fighting capabilities** by enabling quick registration of complaints online, without the need for victims to visit police stations.
 
• This initiative aims to promote **digital transparency, accessibility, and efficiency** in handling cybercrimes across the country.
 
• The platform was developed under the Ministry of Home Affairs as part of the broader effort to modernize India's law enforcement systems to tackle **cyber threats effectively**.
 
• The e-Zero FIR system ensures that the **first information report (FIR)** can be filed remotely, offering greater convenience to victims of cybercrimes and reducing procedural delays.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA):**

 
 
• The MHA is the key ministry responsible for **internal security**, public administration, and law enforcement in India.
 
• It oversees various agencies like **Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)**, **National Investigation Agency (NIA)**, and **Intelligence Bureau (IB)**, which play critical roles in tackling cybercrimes.
 
• The ministry also implements the **National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (cybercrime.gov.in)** to facilitate the online filing of complaints related to cybercrimes.
 
 
 
• **Cybercrime Trends in India:**
 
 
• India has witnessed a significant rise in **cybercrime rates**, including phishing attacks, ransomware, identity theft, and financial fraud.
 
• The government has undertaken various initiatives to strengthen cybersecurity and protect citizens from **digital threats**.
 
 
 
• **Functions of e-Zero FIR:**
 
 
• Allows victims to lodge FIRs online without visiting police stations, ensuring **speedy registration** of complaints.
 
• Enhances accountability and transparency in the **law enforcement process**.
 
• Reduces procedural barriers for reporting cybercrimes, making it more accessible for individuals across the country.
 
 
 
• **Other Cybercrime Initiatives:**
 
 
• The government launched the **Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C)** to address the growing challenge of cyber threats.
 
• The **Cyber Swachhta Kendra** (Botnet Cleaning and Malware Analysis Centre) was established by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) to promote safe and secure internet usage.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• The introduction of e-Zero FIR aligns with the government’s Digital India initiative, which emphasizes **digital empowerment** and modernization of governance systems.
 
• It reflects the growing need for innovative technologies to counter cyber threats and ensure **digital security** for citizens.
